stages.name: Ask
stages.sub: your question → candidate variables → exposure and outcome → a Specifier run · the record appears here
does: A fine-tuned bge-small encoder retrieves a pool of candidate variables. It compares your question with precomputed vectors for every codebook target by cosine similarity and keeps the closest, with no language-model call and no network traffic. It abstains when the best score falls below the shipped threshold. It also refuses to start if the codebook it was built against does not match the one on disk, because a stale vector file would return wrong answers silently.

A language model then reads your question with that pool and decides which candidate is the exposure and which is the outcome. It chooses by index, not by typing a key, so it can only pick from what retrieval returned and can never invent a variable.

This second step exists because an embedding has no sense of direction. Your whole question becomes a single vector, so retrieval cannot tell which construct is the putative cause, and it often returns candidates for only one of the two. Assigning exposure and outcome is therefore the model's job. It proposes the pair and stops; you confirm it.

When you press Run, the Specifier starts. A reasoning call works with the dictionary tools. A MECHANICAL gate then checks that the tool log holds the lookups a defensible record needs. A second, constrained call adds no new facts. Finally the environment overwrites every field it owns and rejects any verdict that contradicts its own log.

The result is the record: the hypothesis, the analysis model and unit of analysis, the covariates adjusted for, excluded on purpose, left undetermined, or sought and not found, the falsifier and its threshold, and estimability with anything blocking it. The record has no study-design field and no typed causal graph; the panel says so beside the record.

stages.name: Query breakdown
stages.sub: what you typed → the one query string the search model sees · no language-model call
does: Turns what you typed into the ONE query string the search model sees. It is plain string concatenation: the same fields always give the same query, with no language model and no network.
request — your words, exactly as typed. construct — what is being searched for, and the only part the search model reads.

role — whether you meant this as the exposure or the outcome. Intake records it and DELIBERATELY leaves it out of the query: the search model turns your words into a single vector and has no notion of cause and effect, so the role would change nothing it does.
instances — concrete examples you named. Intake drops one as covered when all its content words already appear in the construct, so an instance already covered in full is not searched again.
population — left empty by the shipped contract, so nothing here restricts the search to a subgroup.

rendered query — the finished string, assembled as [population] construct [timeframe][: instance, instance, …]. Matching it against the instrument, and deciding which match is the exposure and which the outcome, happens at Ask, not here.

stages.name: Generate
stages.sub: list candidate pairs → prune → screen for estimability → run the Specifier
does: Step S1 lists every candidate exposure–outcome pair, never pairing a construct with itself
Step S2 prunes a pair whose anchor is a free-text answer or whose two anchors sit in the same question battery; a grid battery stays, flagged as needing a derivation
Step S3 screens each pair for estimability, whether its analytic sample size can be estimated; it stays blocked until two survey-metadata exports arrive
Runs the Specifier on a pair the funnel produced, not one you typed

stages.name: Metrics
stages.sub: the one scored run · its ceiling, its bibliography, what it establishes
does: States the ceiling before the score, because the score cannot be read without it
Explains how the scored set was produced, with the gate off, before showing what it scored
Lists the cohort papers the run was scored against, and what each one is
Leaves out the pipeline's own output: the per-record listing and the run's counts are its end-to-end check, and would read as evidence
Reports the retrieval measurements and their known limitations
